In front of the vault is a tray with two bays, pending and claimable. Step {step1}: the investor calls {requestFn}, and the request waits in the pending bay; {pendingFn} returns {amount}. Step {step2}: the vault processes and prices the request, which moves to the claimable bay; {claimableFn} returns {amount} and {pendingFn} zero. Step {step3}: the investor claims with {claimFn} and receives {received}; both view functions return zero for the request. A vault can make a request claimable right away, but the claim is always a separate call.
token-vault-lifecycle-step-idle: Choose a deposit or a redemption and send the request to follow it through its three states.
token-vault-lifecycle-step-request: Step {step}: pending. The investor has called {requestFn}, and the vault holds {amount} for the request: {pendingFn} returns {amount}.
token-vault-lifecycle-step-fulfill: Step {step}: claimable. The vault has processed and priced the request: {claimableFn} returns {amount}, and {pendingFn} zero. The standard defines no event for the change.
token-vault-lifecycle-step-claim: Step {step}: claimed. The investor calls {claimFn} and receives {received}; both view functions return zero for this request.
wallet-keys-caption: One-way steps: the recovery phrase makes your private key, the private key makes your public key, and the public key makes your address.
wallet-keys-description: Four cards sit in a row, joined left to right by arrows: a recovery phrase, a private key, a public key and an address. Each arrow runs one way: going forward is quick, going back is impossible. There are three views. Make the keys: in step {step1}, the wallet turns the recovery phrase of {words} words into a private key of {privateBytes} bytes; in step {step2}, cryptographic math turns the private key into a public key of {publicBytes} bytes; in step {step3}, the address is taken from the last {bytes} bytes of the public key's Keccak-256 hash. Who can see this: a dashed zone marks the public key and the address as safe to share, and another marks the private key and the recovery phrase as secret, because anyone who has either one controls the funds. Try going backward: each arrow is tried in reverse, from the address back to the recovery phrase, and each one is blocked. A real wallet makes many accounts from one recovery phrase; the figure shows one. The key values shown are made-up examples.
wallet-keys-definition-phrase: {words} ordinary words your wallet shows you when you create it. They can rebuild your keys, so keep them offline and private.
wallet-keys-definition-private-key: A secret number that signs your transactions. Whoever has it controls the account's funds.
wallet-keys-definition-public-key: Made from the private key. It lets anyone check your signatures without learning your private key.
wallet-keys-definition-address: The last {bytes} bytes of the public key's hash, written in hex. Share it to receive funds.
wallet-keys-definition-secret: Anyone with your recovery phrase or private key controls your funds. Never share them.
wallet-keys-definition-shareable: Safe to show anyone: your address, to receive funds, and your public key, to check your signatures.
wallet-keys-step-forward-idle: Press Play to watch one recovery phrase become a private key, a public key and an address.
wallet-keys-step-forward-private-key: Step {step}: your wallet turns the recovery phrase into a private key. The same phrase always gives the same key.
wallet-keys-step-forward-public-key: Step {step}: the private key makes the public key using cryptographic math. Easy this way, impossible to undo.
wallet-keys-step-forward-address: Step {step}: your address is the last {bytes} bytes of the public key's Keccak-256 hash. This is what you share.
wallet-keys-step-visibility-idle: Press Play to see which parts you can share and which must stay secret.
wallet-keys-step-visibility-shareable: Step {step}: your address is public. Share it so people can send you funds. Your public key isn't secret either.
wallet-keys-step-visibility-secret: Step {step}: your private key must stay secret. Anyone who has it can sign transactions and take your funds.
wallet-keys-step-visibility-phrase: Step {step}: keep your recovery phrase secret too. It rebuilds your private key, so whoever has it controls your funds.
wallet-keys-step-backward-idle: Press Play to try running the arrows backward, from the address to the recovery phrase.
wallet-keys-step-backward-address: Step {step}: from the address back to the public key? Blocked. A hash can't be run in reverse.
wallet-keys-step-backward-public-key: Step {step}: from the public key back to the private key? Blocked. No known method can work it out in any realistic time.
wallet-keys-step-backward-private-key: Step {step}: from the private key back to the recovery phrase? Blocked too. Every arrow runs one way only.
wallet-keys-status-visibility-shareable: Safe to share: address and public key
wallet-keys-status-backward-public-key: Public key to private key: blocked
wallet-keys-status-backward-private-key: Private key to recovery phrase: blocked
